title: Google My Business API Access and Setup for Developers
summary: The Google My Business API now requires Google's approval before any requests will work. It's split into separate free Business Profile APIs.
body_markdown:
## Access, OAuth and a first working request


Until approval, no request works. After it, the path is short: submit the access request for your Cloud project, enable each API, create an OAuth client with the` business.manage` scope, then call` accounts.list` and` locations.list` .


Every line of code sits downstream of approval.


The sequence runs verify the Business Profile, create the project, submit the form, enable the APIs, configure consent, so a failure at step three surfaces as a quota error at step four. Each stage below leaves something you can check.


### Stage 1: Submit the access request


Start with a Business Profile that's verified, then create a Google Cloud project and copy its project number. Submit the API access request form with that number, a contact address on the business's domain, and a plain description of the use case.


Until Google approves, the project's quota page shows no usable capacity. Code that passes review and still fails on its first call is usually a project that was never approved.


Check the Quotas page for the project; when it shows real capacity for the Business Profile APIs, this stage is done.


### Stage 2: Enable the APIs in Cloud console


Open the API Library on the approved project and enable each API you call. Enabling one doesn't enable the others.


For this walkthrough you need the Account Management API and the Business Information API.


Enabling a single API and then calling a method that belongs to another returns an error that looks like an auth fault but it's a disabled service. Confirm both appear under Enabled APIs before you move on.


### Create the OAuth client and access token


Configure the consent screen first, then create an OAuth client ID. Request one scope:` https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage` .


Sign in as a user who manages the profile, complete the consent flow, and exchange the authorization code for an access token.


Ask for offline access if a server will call later, or the token expires with nobody present to renew it. The token works only for accounts that user manages, so test with that same user.


### List Business Profile accounts and locations


Call` accounts.list` on the Account Management API with the bearer token. The response gives each account a` name` such as` accounts/123` . Pass that value as the parent in` locations.list` on the Business Information API.


Send the request without` readMask` and it is rejected, because the parameter is required. Start with` name,title,storeCode` , then add fields as you need them.


Locations returned with those fields mean access, enablement and OAuth are all working, and you can start reading each API's quota page against your real call volume.


You don't need to hire a developer for the request itself: describe it in the[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) built-in chat, say "list my locations every morning and write them to a sheet", and what it publishes is a live flow in your account, the same one a builder would have assembled by hand.


That flow runs under the same RBAC and audit logs as any other, and its run trace lists the exact resource names sent to Google and the response that came back, so an unapproved project shows up as a rejected first call you can read line by line.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.
